Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.

1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today, is taken on record.

2. The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus commanding respondent No. 4 i.e. Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority to take appropriate action and proceed for execution of compromise sale-deed of Gata No. 188-m & 206-m of revenue village Fatahpur Atta,
Pargana Dankaur, Tehsil & District Gautam Buddh Nagar; to decide the petitioners' application dated 29.09.2022, in which, the same prayer for execution of sale-deed has been made; and not to Mushtaq Ali And 3 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 9 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93314828/
1 interfere in the possession of the petitioners in respect of Gata No. 188-m & 206-m of revenue village Fatahpur Atta, Pargana Dankaur, Tehsil & District Gautam Buddh Nagar, till the execution of compromise sale-deed.

sentences.text: 3. The case of the petitioners is that the State of U.P. issued notifications under Sections 4 & 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for acquisition of the aforesaid land of the petitioners and adjoining lands for planned development in district Gautam Buddh Nagar.

The petitioners claim that they were owners of Gata No. 208 (area 0.7799), Gata No. 188 (area 1.1056) and Gata No. 206 (area 0.5838) admeasuring 2.4693 hectare out of which only 1.7847 hectare was acquired and the petitioners were also paid compensation for the same.
The remaining part i.e. area measuring 0.6846 hectare was not acquired.
The same is comprised of 0.2347 hectare of Gata No. 188m and 0.4498 hectare of Gata No. 206m.
The petitioners are using the remaining land aforesaid for their residence but the respondents are wrongly interfering in the possession of the petitioners.

In case the respondents intend to use the remaining land of the petitioners, they should obtain sale-deed from the petitioners in respect of the said land or else they should not interfere in their possession.

4. The respondent Authority has filed a counter affidavit and it transpires therefrom that a notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued on 13.01.2011 followed by notification dated 24.03.2011 under Section 6 of the Act.
The possession of the acquired lands was taken on 03.06.2011 and award was declared on 13.12.2013.
It is stated that after issuance of notifications, there was change in gata numbers during consolidation operations.
The notifications under Sections 4 & 6 were issued showing old gata numbers as were in existence before the consolidation.

Gata No. 188, which came into existence after consolidation operations, comprised of the following old gata numbers as per CH Form 41 :-
Old Gata No. Area (In Hectare) 316/1 Mi.
0.0050 316/2 Mi.
0.1013 317 Mi.
0.0632 318/2 Mi.
0.1897 319/2 Mi.
0.6325 320 Mi.
0.0698 321/2 Mi.
0.0443 Total 1.1058
The total area of newly carved out Plot No. 188 was 1.5056 hectare out of which 1.1058 hectare came to be recorded in the name of the petitioners.

2 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It also appears from the entries in CH Form 41 that newly constituted Plot No. 206 comprised of the following old gata numbers :-
317 Mi.
0.1316 318/2 Mi.
0.1746 319/2 Mi.
0.1562 320 Mi.
0.0506 373 Mi.
0.0329 374 Mi 0.0379 Total 0.5838
As per C.H. Form 41, the total area of newly carved out Plot No. 206 was 0.5838 hectare, the entire area of which was recorded in the name of the petitioners.

6. Further case of the Authority is that the petitioners were paid compensation for an area admeasuring 1.1058 hectare of Gata No. 188 and entire area of Gata No. 206 i.e. total area 1.7847 hectare which is also admitted to the petitioners in para-6 of the rejoinder affidavit.

In respect of remaining area i.e. 0.6846 hectare, there is a dispute relating to apportionment between the petitioners, Mustaq, Pappu, Altaf & Taj Mohammad, and Smt. Asgari alias Chandri W/o Abdul Waheed with Ali Sher, Kallu Khan, Manna Khan S/o Zabar Khan (Chak Holder No. 99) and therefore, the dispute was referred for adjudication to the Civil Court under Section 30 of the Act by letter dated 17.07.2014 and the petitioners would be paid compensation in terms of the determination made by the civil court.
Since the said determination has not been made so far and therefore, it is not possible to pay any amount to the petitioners for the remaining area.

7. The main crux of argument of learned counsel for the petitioners is that the remaining area of Gata No. 188m i.e. an area measuring 0.2347 hectare and Gata No. 206m measuring 4.4498 hectare was not acquired and therefore, the respondents if they intend to use it should acquire title over it by getting a sale-deed executed in their favour.
8.
However, as noted above, we find that the entire area of newly constituted Gata No. 188m as well as Gata No. 206 was duly acquired.

Although in respect of part of the area, the compensation amount has not been paid to the petitioners in view of dispute of apportionment raised by the tenure holders of Chak No. 99 i.e. Ali Sher and others.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioners tried to contend that they had not received any notice relating to pendency of the reference before civil court.
This, in our opinion, would not entitle them to the relief claimed, once the case of the petitioners that 0.6846 hectare of their land was not acquired, is not found to be correct.
The alleged claim of the petitioners, based on possession in the context of the relief sought, is also not sustainable.

3 10.

sentences.text: Since the dispute relating to apportionment has been referred to the civil court, we leave it open to the petitioners to contest the said proceedings and pray to the court concerned for its expeditious disposal.
It goes without saying that dependant upon the outcome of the said proceedings, the respondents will take decision regarding disbursement of compensation amount.
11. The petition stands disposed of with the above observation.
